title: Takeshita Street gate, Harajuku
lede: The entrance arch of Harajuku’s Takeshita Street in 2024, crowned with a balloon rabbit, stars, and sparkles above daisy-patterned posts.
summary: Street gate with a pink-and-white balloon rabbit, stars, and sparkles over a busy shopping street. Harajuku, Tokyo, photographed 2024.

creator.name: Jakub Hałun (photograph); gate and decoration by unrecorded makers

evidence.note: Inspected the Commons photograph by Jakub Hałun at 1280 × 1930 px. Also compared a [CC0 photograph by Syced from November 2024](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Takeshita_Street.jpg), in which the balloon rabbit is gone and the arch carries a pink banner reading “かわいいがすぎる〜” with two dot-eyed characters.

styles.note: Partial fit: the gate decoration is kawaii (a dot-eyed rabbit, stars, sparkles, daisies, pink and white), but the surrounding street is a mixed commercial scene.

context: Takeshita Street is a street in Harajuku, Tokyo (Wikidata Q3179287). The photographer describes the image as “Takeshita street, Harajuku, Tokyo” and dates it 22 August 2024. [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Takeshita_street,_Tokyo,_20240822_1032_5383.jpg).

The gate decoration changes over time: the November 2024 photograph by Syced shows a printed banner in place of the balloon figure. [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Takeshita_Street.jpg).
observed: A steel arch spans the street on two posts decorated with small white daisy shapes; the words “Takeshita Street” sit above a light box.
On top, a rabbit built from white and pink balloons has dot eyes and a small smiling mouth; it rises out of a burst of pink and red balloons.
Yellow and blue stars made of balloons and red four-pointed sparkle shapes surround the rabbit.
Under the light box hangs an anime banner with six large-eyed characters.
Beyond the gate, a narrow pedestrian street is crowded with umbrellas, shop signs, and a McDonald’s sign.
interpretation: The gate is kawaii at street scale: one friendly face, scattered stars and sparkles, and a pink-and-white palette, used to mark the entrance to a youth shopping street.
The temporary balloon figure shows how the style is used for seasonal, changeable decoration rather than permanent architecture.
borrow: Mark an entrance or a page header with one character and a scatter of stars and four-pointed sparkles.
Use a small repeated flower shape as a pattern on a plain structural element.

images.alt: A shopping street seen through a steel arch. On top of the arch, a rabbit made of white and pink balloons, with dot eyes and a small smile, is surrounded by balloon stars in yellow and blue and red sparkle shapes. The words Takeshita Street sit above a light box and an anime banner. People with umbrellas walk down the narrow street between shop signs.
images.caption: Takeshita Street gate, Harajuku, 22 August 2024. Photograph by Jakub Hałun, [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Takeshita_street,_Tokyo,_20240822_1032_5383.jpg). Incidental: an anime banner with six characters, shop signs, and a McDonald’s sign. Stored from the 1280 px Commons thumbnail.

rights.statement: Photograph © Jakub Hałun, CC BY 4.0, own work per Wikimedia Commons. The main subject is a public street and its gate. The balloon rabbit is a street decoration, not a licensed character; the anime banner and shop signs are incidental third-party works. Japanese copyright law (Article 46) allows photographs of works permanently installed outdoors, but the balloon figure was temporary, so the lead curator should confirm the tier.
